name: Equatorial Guinea
snapshot: Ruled since 1979 by Teodoro Obiang, the world's longest-serving president, whose son and heir announced in June 2026 that the whole cabinet had resigned for missing its targets.
culture: Equatorial Guinea is the only African country where Spanish is an official language, alongside French and Portuguese. The capital, Malabo, is on Bioko island, home to the Bubi people, while most of the population lives on the mainland, where the Fang are the largest group. Catholic festivals and traditional balélé dances mark the calendar.
society: Oil discovered in the 1990s made the country briefly one of the richest per head in Africa, but wealth was concentrated in the ruling family; the vice-president, Obiang's son, has been convicted in France of embezzlement. Output has declined. Basic services remain poor and press freedom is among the world's lowest.
situation: Obiang won a sixth term in 2022 with an officially reported 95 percent, and his son Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, known as Teodorín, is vice-president and presumed successor. In 2026 the government announced the capital will move from Malabo to Ciudad de la Paz on the mainland, Pope Leo XIV visited in April, and in June Teodorín announced that the entire cabinet had resigned after meeting only a tenth of its goals. Rights groups have challenged the forced return of migrants deported to the country by the United States.
power: A presidential republic in form and a family dictatorship in practice. The president appoints the government and controls the security forces; the ruling PDGE holds nearly every seat in parliament.

leaders.state: President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, since 1979
leaders.gov: Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue; Prime Minister Manuel Osa Nsue Nsua's cabinet resigned in June 2026
